description: Search or list the public archive of The Durability Curve: essays on which kinds of work keep their value as AI gets cheaper, the checked claims in each essay's claim ledger, the dated calls printed in The Durability Curve Weekly, the five laws and two derived principles the essays are tested against, the free tools, and AI model releases. With a query, returns ranked matches, each with its kind (essay, claim, call, law, tool or model), a snippet and a URL (canonical for essay citations); "title_matched" says whether any essay title contains every word of the query, and "none_found" is true when nothing matches enough of the query (the nearest misses are then under "closest", not "results"). With an empty query, lists newest first, filtered by kind, series, has_ledger or access, and "total" counts every match. Read a match in full with get_essay, get_claim_ledger, get_weekly_calls or get_ai_models. These tools retrieve The Durability Curve's public material. They do not certify that any claim is true.

access.description: Only essays a reader of durabilitycurve.com gets in full ("free") or only in part ("part paid": the rest is for paid subscribers).

has_ledger.description: true: only essays that have a claim ledger. false: only essays without one.

kind.description: Only this kind of result: essay, claim, call, law (the framework's laws and principles), tool (the free tools) or model (AI model releases). A list (empty query) defaults to essays.

limit.description: How many results to return, 1 to 25. Default 5.

query.description: What to look for, in plain words, e.g. "agent reliability", "memory chip deposits", a call ID like "W02-5" or a model name like "Claude Opus 5.5". Leave empty to LIST instead (newest first), with the filters below.

series.description: Only essays (and their claims) in this series, e.g. "The Blueprint". Case does not matter.

sort.description: relevance (default for a query) or newest. A list is always newest first.

name: search
title: Search The Durability Curve
